title: Odo's Wobbly Reflections
markdown:
Sunbeams giggled on dewdrops in Sunny Meadow Garden. Today was the Grand Garden Silliest Reflection Contest, and every creature with a puddle, a dewdrop, or a shiny mushroom cap had come to show off.

Hazel the bunny hopped with twitchy ears and a wiggling nose. “What splendid silliness this will be,” she chirped, light as a dandelion puff.

Her best friend, Odo the goldfish, blew a bubbly sigh from his lily-pad pond. His orange scales shone like a tiny sun. “I do wish I could see the funny reflections, Hazel. But my pond is so watery. Everything looks wobbly and bubbly, like a giant upside-down jelly.” He peered at his own round face. It looked like a Wiggly-Woo.

Hazel’s ears rose like two happy flags. “Do not worry your bubbly head. We will be the bestest judges. You tell me what you see. I will make sure you can see it.”

Odo could not leave the pond, though. Therefore Hazel hopped to the garden edge and found a big flat pebble, worn smooth by rain and wind. She set it at the very brim. “A peeking place. No wobbles right there.”

The water still threw the world about. Therefore she gathered the shiniest, wobbliest, wiggly leaves and floated them on the surface. “These will catch the sunshine and bounce the light. Extra bright for official silliness-spotters.”

“Hooray,” Odo bubbled, flipping. He swam to the pebble-seat and peered. “Wowee. It is so much clearer. I can see. I can really see.”

The contest began, and Hazel hopped from puddle to puddle so Odo would not miss a single entry.

A plump, proud robin fluttered past. Its reflection in a dewdrop on a spiderweb looked like a tiny flying teacup with wings, round as a biscuit and twice as pleased with itself.

“Silly,” giggled Odo, bubbles dancing. Silly, wobbly, Wiggly-Woo.

Next, a snail named Slimy Silas slimed, ever so slowly, across a shiny emerald mushroom. His reflection stretched long and wiggly, like a moving ribbon sliding down a green hill. Silas did not hurry. The reflection did not mind.

“Hilarious,” Odo said, wiggling himself. “He looks as if he is on a slide.” Silly, wobbly, Wiggly-Woo.

Hazel darted this way and that, nose twitching, eyes wide with searching. She found a dandelion puff in a shallow puddle, its white seeds like a dozen bouncing clouds huddled together, as if they had come to the contest as a team.

“That is so funny,” Odo declared, voice full of delight.

Then they saw a big bumpy stone near soft moss. The puddle beside it made a lumpy monster with a very sour face.

Odo blinked. A worried frown. “Oh dear. That one looks a bit much. It looks so grumpy. Am I judging it right, Hazel? Does it have to look like a grumpy old rock monster?”

Hazel nudged his pebble-seat with her soft side. “It is the silliest reflection contest, remember. Sometimes silly looks a little grumpy. You keep being you. Your eyes are the best for spotting silliness.”

Odo felt a warm bubble of confidence. He looked again. With Hazel’s words in his fins, the lumpy reflection became a giant sleepy potato with a frown.

Silly, wobbly, Wiggly-Woo.

They kept their important judging. A ladybug wore a spot that winked like a tiny bright eye in a perfectly round water droplet, as if it were telling a joke only puddles understood. Then came a shy frog whose happy croak made its reflection jump much higher than the real frog. The reflection was showing off. The frog looked faintly embarrassed, which made Odo giggle harder.

The sun dipped and painted the garden gold. Near a patch of bright clover, tucked away as if it had been waiting, a slender blade of grass held a perfect shimmering water bead on its tip. A breeze rustled through the garden. The grass wiggled and jiggled. The bead threw a tiny dancing rainbow onto the shiny wing of a passing beetle. The whole miniature display looked like a wobbly circus act happening right before their eyes: light, water, movement, all in one breath.

Odo shouted and blew bubbles that popped like tiny fireworks. “That is it. The silliest, sparkliest, wobbliest, wiggly-est reflection of all. It is the winner.”

Hazel thumped her hind foot, a happy drumbeat. “You found the silliest of them all.”

Garden creatures gathered and cheered with paws, wings, and feelers. Sunshine seemed a little brighter. Hazel’s giggles mixed with Odo’s joyful bubbles.

Odo, the shy goldfish, sat tall on his pebble-seat, prouder than a peacock, still a Wiggly-Woo, and perfectly pleased about it.
